Action: # Article References: Article References
article_references/article_references
## Preparation
Setup: Ensure that the publisher account owns a journal for example with Print ISSN "1111-1111" and E-ISSN "2222-2222", and these are not attached to any other journals
Setup: You must be logged in using a publisher account

Go to the "Upload Article XML" tab in the "Publisher Area" and upload the test resource file "with_references.xml" using the "DOAJ Native XML" format

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//publisher/uploadfile

Test Resource: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DOAJ/doaj/feature/3985_references_article_metadata/doajtest/xml_upload_test_package/DOAJ/with_references.xml
wait a short amount of time for the job to process, then reload the page (do not re-submit the form data).  If the job remains in "pending", reload the page until the status changes.

Expected Test Results: Your file is shown in the "History of uploads" with status "successfully processed", and the Note "1 articles imported (1 new, 0 updated)"

Action:
Go to the Table of Contents for the journal at /toc/2222-2222, go to the Articles tab and open the article "References!".  Make a note of the article id in the URL, you will need it for the following tests.

http://testdoaj.cottagelabs.com//toc/2222-2222

Expected Test Results: The article page for "References!" is shown

Action: ## References are displayed on the article page

Step Number: Depends on Article References : Article References : Preparation

Action: Open the public article page for the article "References!" as an anonymous user

Expected Test Results: A "References" section with the heading "References" is shown
The 4 references are shown as a numbered list, in the same order as in the uploaded file

Action: Check the first reference, which contains the DOI "10.1234/abc"

Expected Test Results: The DOI is displayed as a link
Clicking the link opens https://doi.org/10.1234/abc in a new tab

Action: Check the second reference, which contains the URL "https://www.doaj.org/"

Expected Test Results: The URL is displayed as a link
Clicking the link opens the URL in a new tab

Action: Check the third reference, which contains no DOI and no URL

Expected Test Results: The reference is displayed as plain text with no links

Action: Check the fourth reference, which contains the text "markup"

Expected Test Results: The reference text is displayed exactly as it was supplied: Taylor, C. (2023) A reference with markup in it.
No part of the reference is rendered as italics, and no part of the page layout is broken

Action: Open the public article page of an article which has no references (e.g. an article uploaded from "successful.xml")

Expected Test Results: No "References" heading and no reference list is shown on the page

Action: ## References are available in the public API

Step Number: Depends on Article References : Article References : Preparation

Action: Request the article from the API, using the article id noted in the Preparation test, by going to /api/articles/{article_id}

Expected Test Results: The JSON response contains a "bibjson.reference" array with the 4 references, as strings, in the order they were uploaded

Action: Search for the article via the API search endpoint, e.g. /api/search/articles/bibjson.title:%22References!%22

Expected Test Results: The article in the results contains the same "bibjson.reference" array

Action: ## References are available in OAI-PMH

Step Number: Depends on Article References : Article References : Preparation

Action: Request the article record in the DOAJ OAI-PMH format, by going to /oai.article?verb=GetRecord&metadataPrefix=oai_doaj&identifier=oai:doaj.org/article:{article_id}

Expected Test Results: The record contains a "<references>" element with one "<reference>" element per reference, in the order they were uploaded
The reference containing markup is correctly escaped in the XML, and the XML is well formed

Action: Request the same record in the Dublin Core format, by going to /oai.article?verb=GetRecord&metadataPrefix=oai_dc&identifier=oai:doaj.org/article:{article_id}

Expected Test Results: The record is returned successfully (references are not part of the Dublin Core format)

Action: ## References are available in the RIS export

Step Number: Depends on Article References : Article References : Preparation

Action: Download the RIS export of the article, using the article id noted in the Preparation test, by going to /service/export/article/{article_id}/ris

Expected Test Results: A RIS file is downloaded

Action: Open the downloaded file in a text editor

Expected Test Results: There is one "CR  -" line for each of the 4 references, in the order they were uploaded
The rest of the RIS record (TY, TI, AU, etc.) is unchanged

Action: ## References are shown in the article metadata form

Step Number: Depends on Article References : Article References : Preparation

Action: Go to the "Enter Article Metadata" tab in the "Publisher Area"
Find the "References" field

Expected Test Results: The field is a multi-line textarea
The help text reads: One reference per line

Action: Fill in the required fields for a new article (title, author, Full-Text URL and the journal ISSNs) and enter 3 references in the "References" field, one per line, leaving a blank line between two of them
Click "Add Article"

Expected Test Results: At the top of the page you see the confirmation message: Article created/updated

Action: Open the public page of the article you have just created

Expected Test Results: The 3 references are shown in the "References" section, in the order you entered them
The blank line has not created an empty reference

Action: Create another article without entering anything in the "References" field, then open its public page

Expected Test Results: No "References" section is shown
